High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 907 of 2022

Applicant :- Smt. Aneeta And Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And
Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Puneet Bhadauria,Ajay Kumar Pandey,Yatish Kumar Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Raghuvansh Chandra,Ram Jee Saxena

Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and
perused the record.

2.  This application has been moved on behalf of the applicants- Smt. Aneeta and Km. Preeti seeking anticipatory bail during trial in Sessions Trial No.409 of 2020, under sections- 149 and 313 I.P.C.
only based on Complaint Case No.663 of 2019, under sections- 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and sections- 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Garhmukteshwar, District- Hapur.
3. It is contended on behalf of the applicants that they were initially summoned in the aforesaid complaint case under sections- 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and sections- 3/4 D.P. Act.

It is brought to the notice of the Court that in the above complaint case only one person, the husband of the complainant- Mikin Brahmi was summoned for offence under sections 149 and 313 I.P.C. in addition to sections- 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and sections- 3/4 D.P. Act and the case was committed to the Court of Session.
The Court of Session framed charges in additional sections- 313 and 149 I.P.C. against all the accused persons including the present applicants.

It is argued that though the applicants are on bail under sections- 323, 498A, 504, 506 I.P.C. and sections- 3/4 D.P.
Smt. Aneeta And Another vs State Of U.P.And Another on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36484339/
1 Act, however without any cogent reason and without any speaking order, they have been charged in additional sections of 313 and 149 I.P.C.

entities.text:
D.P.
Smt. Aneeta And Another vs State Of U.P.And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present applicants have already been granted an interim protection by this Court and they have not breached any of the conditions imposed on them.
Hence, they are liable to be granted anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.

4. The application for anticipatory bail is opposed by the learned A.G.A.
5.

It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

9. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion at any stage of the case Smt.
